nodes.content: Design a multi-region secret broker reconciling emergency credential revocation, partition availability, and rollback-safe rotation.
requirements: Revoked credentials become unusable within 60 seconds, including during network partitions and broker replica rollback.
Unrevoked workloads maintain 99.9% authentication success during 30-second regional partitions overlapping credential rotation.

nodes.content: Use 10-second signed freshness heartbeats, 45-second hardware-fenced authorization leases, rollback-proof revocation floors, and pre-staged overlapping regional rotation keys.
How can rolled-back replicas reject replayed authorization leases while accepting pre-staged rotation keys during a 30-second partition?
TPM revocation floors reject stale-epoch replay; 50-second checkpoint-capped leases and overlapping keys yield ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% partition authentication.
Run PartitionRoll-30 with 30-second partitions, replica rollback, revocation, and overlapping-key rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
PartitionRoll-30 observed revoked_accept_seconds ≤49 after rollback and unrevoked_auth_success 99.96% across 30-second rotation partitions.
Adopt TPM-fenced revocation floors and pre-staged overlapping keys; PartitionRoll-30 met both revocation and partition-availability thresholds.
Canary TPM-fenced revocation floors, checkpoint-capped leases, and overlapping keys; promote regions only at ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
Deploy Canary-R1 across two regions; inject partition and broker rollback during rotation, recording revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
Canary-R1 rollout bundle contains TPM-fenced revocation policy, overlapping-key rotation manifests, and revoked_accept_seconds/unrevoked_auth_success dashboards.
Verifier-side TPM-clock-checked 50-second tickets, refreshed every 10 seconds, reject expired rollback replays; overlapping keys preserve partition authentication.
Run TicketReplay-30 with verifier rollback, 30-second partitions, revocation, and rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
TicketReplay-30 measured unrevoked_auth_success 98.8% after verifier rollback: 25-second TPM-clock offset expired tickets midpartition.
Use verifier-local TPM monotonic deadlines and persistent revocation floors for 45-second leases, with pre-staged overlapping rotation keys.
Implement TPM-monotonic 45-second lease deadlines, persistent revocation floors, regional renewals, and overlapping keys; rerun TicketReplay-30 against both SLOs.
Use Canary-R1 rollout bundle to compare heartbeat-fenced leases against TPM-monotonic deadlines in TicketReplay-30; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
TicketReplay-30: heartbeat expiry reduced unrevoked_auth_success to 98.7%; TPM-monotonic reached 99.95%, with revoked_accept_seconds 44 under rollback.
How can regional lease renewals avoid extending unseen revocations beyond 60 seconds when revocation begins during a partition?
Ten-second checkpoint freshness and renewal cadence with 45-second TPM leases should yield revoked_accept_seconds ≤55 and unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Sweep revocation onset around 10-second checkpoint and renewal boundaries during RenewalWindow-30 partitions, rollback, and rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
RenewalWindow-30 boundary sweep measured revoked_accept_seconds 54 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.94% during 30-second partitions with rollback and rotation.
Run RenewalWindow-30 with checkpoints delayed nine seconds before partition onset; test renewal-boundary revocations and measure both SLO metrics.
RenewalWindow-30 delayed-checkpoint run measured revoked_accept_seconds 63, exceeding the 60-second limit; unrevoked_auth_success remained 99.93%.
Cap regional renewals at 50 seconds from the last globally verified checkpoint; predict revoked_accept_seconds ≤59 and unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Use baseline and delayed-checkpoint RenewalWindow-30 traces to test 50-second globally verified checkpoint caps; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
RenewalWindow-30 baseline and delayed-checkpoint traces showed revoked_accept_seconds ≤59 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.92% with checkpoint-capped renewals.
Adopt 50-second checkpoint-capped renewals: baseline passed, delayed uncapped revocation took 63 seconds, and capped runs met both thresholds.
Roll out checkpoint-capped TPM renewals with pre-staged rotation keys; gate promotion on revoked_accept_seconds ≤60 and unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Apply Canary-R1 bundle to deploy checkpoint-capped TPM renewals; inject delayed checkpoints, 30-second partitions, rotation, revocation, and rollback.
Canary-R2 bundle replaces Canary-R1’s lease policy with TPM-monotonic checkpoint-capped renewals and delayed-checkpoint revocation/availability gates.
Move authorization to workload sidecars using TPM-fenced 40-second offline grants and prepublished next-key sets for partition-tolerant rotation.
Prototype sidecar grants with durable revocation floors and overlapping keys; benchmark revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success against Canary-R2.
Use Canary-R2's harness to compare broker and sidecar grants during delayed checkpoints, rollback, 30-second partitioned rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
SidecarBench-30 measured revoked_accept_seconds 48 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.97%, versus Canary-R2’s 59 and 99.92%.
Issue nonrenewable 45-second quorum-signed capabilities every five seconds; use TPM-fenced verifier expiry and pre-staged overlapping rotation keys.
How can verifiers authenticate through broker rollback and partitioned rotation without accepting revoked capabilities beyond 60 seconds?
Quorum-signed 45-second capabilities with persistent TPM expiry anchors and overlapping keys should yield revoked_accept_seconds ≤55 and unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Run CapabilityQuorum-30 with issuance-boundary revocation, broker rollback, and partitioned rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
CapabilityQuorum-30 measured unrevoked_auth_success 98.6%: aged capabilities expired before partition healed, blocking quorum reissuance; revoked_accept_seconds was 44.
Sweep capability age (0–45 seconds) at partition onset with verifier rollback and rotation; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
With regional quorum reissuance and checkpoint-capped expiry, the 0–45-second age sweep measured revoked_accept_seconds 54 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.93%.
Regional quorum reissuance of 45-second capabilities, capped 50 seconds after global checkpoints, should yield revoked_accept_seconds ≤59 and unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Replay CapabilityQuorum-30 failure and age-sweep traces with regional quorum reissuance and 50-second checkpoint caps; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
CapabilityQuorum-30 replay achieved revoked_accept_seconds 56 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.94% with regional quorum reissuance and checkpoint caps.
Reject global-only reissuance; adopt regional quorum with checkpoint caps, raising authentication from 98.6% to 99.94% while revocation takes 56 seconds.
Canary regional quorum reissuance with 50-second checkpoint caps and overlapping keys; promote only at ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
Extend Canary-R2 harness with regional quorum reissuance; inject checkpoint delays, broker rollback, revocation, and partitioned rotation across regions.
Canary-R3 bundle replaces Canary-R2 broker renewals with regional quorum capability reissuance, retaining checkpoint caps, overlapping keys, and SLO gates.
Use service-verified, TPM-monotonic 50-second checkpoint-capped mTLS certificates and prepublished dual-key trust bundles, bypassing brokers during partitions.
Prototype checkpoint-capped mTLS and dual-key bundles; compare revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success against Canary-R3 under rollback and partitioned rotation.
Use Canary-R3 harness to compare quorum capabilities versus checkpoint-capped mTLS under 30-second partitioned rotation and rollback; record revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
Canary-R3 comparison measured mTLS revoked_accept_seconds 52 and unrevoked_auth_success 99.98%, versus quorum capabilities’ 56 and 99.94%.
Can checkpoint-capped mTLS retain ≥99.9% authentication when dual-key bundle propagation lags 20 seconds before partitioned rotation?
Publishing next-key bundles 60 seconds before activation should preserve unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9% despite 20-second lag and 30-second partitions.
Replay Canary-R3’s 99.98% mTLS baseline with 60-second prepublication, 20-second bundle lag, and 30-second partitioned rotation; measure unrevoked_auth_success.
BundleLag-30 measured unrevoked_auth_success 99.96% with 60-second prepublication, 20-second propagation lag, and 30-second partitioned rotation.
Gate new-key issuance on regional verifier acknowledgments, retaining old-key issuance during partitions; predict unrevoked_auth_success ≥99.9%.
Run BundleLag-30 with acknowledgment-gated issuance, 20-second bundle lag, and rollback during partitioned rotation; compare unrevoked_auth_success to Canary-R3.
BundleLag-30 measured unrevoked_auth_success 99.72%: rollback erased acknowledgments, leaving old-key certificates unusable after scheduled verifier key retirement.
Adopt 60-second dual-key prepublication: 99.96% authentication under lag, 52-second mTLS revocation; reject acknowledgment gating at 99.72%.
Canary checkpoint-capped mTLS with 60-second dual-key prepublication; require ≥99.9% authentication under 20-second lag and ≤60-second revocation.
Extend Canary-R3 with BundleLag-30’s 60-second prepublication; inject 20-second lag, 30-second partition, revocation, and rollback; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
Canary-R4 bundle replaces Canary-R3 quorum capabilities with checkpoint-capped mTLS and 60-second prepublished dual-key trust bundles; retains rollback and SLO gates.

Compare Canary-R4’s 60-second prepublication against Canary-R3 under 20-second lag, 30-second partitioned rotation, revocation, and rollback; measure revoked_accept_seconds and unrevoked_auth_success.
Lagged-partition canary measured Canary-R4 unrevoked_auth_success 99.95% and revoked_accept_seconds 53, versus Canary-R3’s 99.91% and 56.
Promote Canary-R4 over Canary-R3 and acknowledgment gating: 99.95% authentication, 53-second revocation; lag replay reached 99.96%, gating only 99.72%.
